Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: POPIA gives South African citizens nine data rights including the right to access, correct, and request deletion of their personal information. The Promotion of Access to Information Act (PAIA) 2000 provides a formal mechanism to request personal data held by government. The Identification Act Section 19 provides for correction of ID documentation. The MyMzansi roadmap plans a Credentials Wallet allowing citizens to view and share verified data. Citizens currently can access their data through formal PAIA/POPIA processes.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: South Africa has general judicial oversight through its constitutional courts and the Promotion of Access to Information Act (PAIA) 2000, which allows individuals to challenge government data handling. The Information Regulator (IRSA) provides quasi-judicial oversight of data protection. However, there are no ID-system-specific judicial mechanisms. Courts can adjudicate ID-related disputes but no dedicated ID court or tribunal exists.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Data sharing is partially governed. The Identification Act Section 21 restricts unauthorized access to the NPR, with the Director-General able to approve access for specific purposes. POPIA establishes lawful processing conditions for data sharing. The DHA OIM Policy 2022 acknowledges that rule-based access governed by legislation is the goal, but notes current challenges with ad-hoc 'data dumping' to other government systems contrary to POPIA. Data sharing rules partially available/partially implemented.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: The Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA), Act 4 of 2013, came into full effect on 1 July 2021. It establishes eight conditions for lawful data processing, nine rights for data subjects, and the Information Regulator of South Africa (IRSA) as the enforcement authority. POPIA applies to both public and private bodies processing personal information in South Africa, including identity management systems.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Information Regulator of South Africa (IRSA) was established under POPIA and became operational in 2021. It has broad powers including issuing enforcement notices, conducting investigations, imposing fines up to ZAR 10 million, and receiving complaints from individuals. In April 2025 the IRSA launched a mandatory e-portal for data breach reporting, demonstrating active enforcement. The IRSA has issued enforcement notices to Dis-Chem and SAPS.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The Smart ID card is the official government-issued identity document and constitutes legal proof of identity in South Africa. It is required for registering for matric exams, applying for a driver's license, opening a bank account, accessing social grants, and voting. The Official Identity Management Policy (Cabinet-approved March 2022) positions the DHA as the sole provider of official legal identity documents for citizens and lawful residents.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: A comprehensive legal framework governs South Africa's ID system. Key legislation includes the Identification Act 68 of 1997, the Births and Deaths Registration Act 1992, the Citizenship Act, and the Constitution (Section 28). The Official Identity Management Policy was Cabinet-approved in March 2022. The National Identification and Registration Bill 2023 was gazetted for public comment. POPIA (2013, in force 2021) and PAIA 2000 also govern the framework.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: The Identification Act 68 of 1997 mandates that all South African citizens aged 16 and above must apply for an identity document within 7 days of a request by an authorized official, with failure to apply being a criminal offense (fine or up to 12 months imprisonment per GNR.978 of 1998). All persons required to have an ID must surrender green ID books when issued a Smart ID. Enrollment is effectively mandatory for all eligible citizens.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration is mandatory in South Africa under the Regulation of Interception of Communications and Provision of Communication-Related Information Act (RICA) 2002, effective 2009. All new prepaid and contract SIM cards must be registered with a government-issued ID (SA ID book or card, passport for foreigners) and proof of residence before activation. Network operators cannot activate a SIM without RICA registration. ID use for SIM registration is mandatory.
